record.paper_title: Pole solutions in the case of problems of flame front propagation and Saffman-Teylor "finger" formation without surface tension: open problems and possible ways of their solutions
record.context_brief: Allowed versus singular initial pole conditions
record.original_question: For finite-pole pole solutions of zero-surface-tension channel Laplacian growth, what are the exact necessary conditions that classify an initial pole configuration as allowed, meaning that it does not approach a finite-time singularity, rather than as an initial configuration that leads to a finite-time singularity?

evidence.quote: In our teamwork with Mark Mineev-Weinstein [5] it was shown, that for finite number of poles at almost all allowed (in the sense of not approaching to finite time singularities) initial conditions, except for small number of some degenerated initial conditions, they have asymptotic as some "finger" with any possible thickness.
Exact necessary conditions, whether defining the initial pole condition as "allowed", i.e. singular, is still a open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider two-dimensional Laplacian growth in a channel (the zero-surface-tension Saffman–Taylor problem in a Hele–Shaw cell of finite width with periodic or no-flux lateral boundary conditions). The moving interface separating the inviscid fluid (or burnt region, in the equivalent flame-front formulation) from the viscous fluid is described by a time-dependent conformal map z = f(w,t) from the exterior (or interior) of the unit disk in an auxiliary w-plane onto the physical domain occupied by the displaced fluid. The map is taken in the meromorphic "pole" ansatz

  f(w,t) = w + V(t) + Σ_{k=1}^{N} α_k(t) · log(w − w_k(t)),

where N is a fixed positive integer and {α_k(t), w_k(t)} are the (complex) strengths and locations of a finite number of logarithmic singularities ("poles"). Substituting this ansatz into the zero-surface-tension Laplacian-growth equation yields a finite-dimensional dynamical system for the parameters (α_k(t), w_k(t)).

An initial pole configuration {α_k(0), w_k(0)}_{k=1}^{N} is said to be "allowed" if the resulting solution remains conformal for all t > 0, i.e. the interface develops no finite-time singularity (no cusp formation and no pole crossing the unit circle in finite time); otherwise the configuration is called singular.

Problem. Determine the exact necessary and sufficient conditions on the initial data {α_k(0), w_k(0)}_{k=1}^{N} that characterize the set of allowed configurations (those whose evolution under the pole dynamics never reaches a finite-time singularity).
artifact.status_search_result: Available literature on pole dynamics in zero-surface-tension Laplacian growth (Mineev-Weinstein, Dawson, and collaborators) gives sufficient conditions ensuring non-singular evolution (e.g. restricting pole strengths and excluding certain pole configurations) and shows that generic non-singular initial data produce an asymptotic half-width finger, but no complete necessary-and-sufficient characterization of the set of allowed initial pole configurations appears to have been established; the problem is generally treated as open in subsequent work.

status_evidence.title: Dynamics of Finger Formation in Laplacian Growth Without Surface Tension
status_evidence.snippet: Exact non-singular zero-surface tension solutions in which logarithmic poles are repelled from the origin and attracted to the unit circle; configurations producing finite-time singularities are excluded.
status_evidence.claim: Sufficient (not necessary) conditions for avoiding finite-time singularities are given, indicating the full classification remains incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Selection of the Saffman-Taylor Finger Width in the Absence of Surface Tension: An Exact Result
status_evidence.snippet: Solutions free of finite-time singularities asymptote to a single finger whose width depends on initial conditions, while many meromorphic solutions lose conformality through cusps.
status_evidence.claim: Distinguishing allowed from singular initial pole data is identified as a delicate, unresolved issue.
